harbour.aliases.customKeywords: Custom words that should be colored as a keyword when they start a statement (e.g. a word defined via your own #command/#xtranslate macro)
harbour.aliases.customKeywords.word: The word to color as a keyword (case-insensitive)
harbour.aliases.customKeywords.scope: Which highlight color/scope to use for this word
harbour.aliases.callSuffixes: Method-call suffixes (e.g. "Exec") that should be treated as calling the receiver identifier directly, so that signature help and completion for `identifier:Suffix(...)` behave like `identifier(...)`
harbour.aliases.callSuffixMode: For functions defined in the workspace, whether to allow calling them both as `name(...)` and `name:Suffix(...)` ("either", default), require the suffix form ("suffixOnly"), or forbid it ("bareOnly"). Violations are reported as Error diagnostics. Has no effect if harbour.aliases.callSuffixes is empty; never applies to standard RTL functions.
harbour.aliases.commandRules: Custom #command rules (e.g. your own DEFAULT/translate macros) applied automatically to every file, without having to paste a #command line at the top of each .prg. Each rule is compiled into a generated .ch file that is passed to the compiler with -u+. The first word of 'match' is also colored as a keyword automatically.
harbour.aliases.commandRules.match: The pattern to match, using standard xHarbour #command syntax (e.g. "DEFAULT <v> := <x>")
harbour.aliases.commandRules.replace: What the matched pattern expands to (e.g. "Default( <v>, <x> )")
harbour.aliases.customDefault: Built-in support for the DEFAULT command (e.g. "Default cNome := \"mundo\""), including cascading multiple assignments in one statement with ",;" line continuation (e.g. "Default cNome := x, cSobrenome := y"), with no #command/commandRules setup needed. Also colors DEFAULT like a keyword. On by default; set to false to turn it off (e.g. if your own harbour.aliases.commandRules defines a conflicting DEFAULT command).
harbour.aliases.commandRulesUseFileDir: Where to write the generated .ch file for commandRules/customDefault: the OS temp dir (default, keeps it out of your project folder) or, if enabled, next to the file being compiled. Only enable this if harbour.compilerExecutable is a wrapper (e.g. a Docker container) that can't see the OS temp dir -- otherwise leave it off.
harbour.iconTheme.baseIconTheme: id of another installed File Icon Theme (e.g. "catppuccin-mocha") whose icons the "xHarbour Icons" theme should also show for every other file type, so activating xHarbour Icons doesn't lose your current theme's icons -- only .prg/.ch/.hbx/.hb get the xHarbour icon added on top. Leave empty to use plain generic file/folder icons for everything else instead. Changing this requires reloading the window to take effect.
harbour.iconTheme.reloadPrompt: Reload the window for the xHarbour Icons theme to pick up the new base icon theme.
harbour.validating: Every time a file is opened or saved the executable is called to validate the code(Lint)
harbour.compilerExecutable: complete path of the harbour executable
harbour.extraOptions: other options to pass to harbour compiler
harbour.extraIncludePaths: Extra include paths to use during the compilation (for include)
harbour.decorator: Enables the decoration of correspondents if/endif, for/next, while/endwhile, etc etc
harbour.checkUndefinedFunctions: Shows an informational hint on calls to functions not found anywhere in the indexed workspace nor in the standard xHarbour/Harbour RTL. Off by default. Only takes effect when harbour.workspaceDepth is greater than 0: with depth 0 the language server only knows about files you've actually opened, so almost any cross-file call would be flagged. Functions defined in an external library that isn't part of the workspace will still be flagged, since the language server has no visibility into it.
harbour.workspaceDepth: How many sub-folder levels below the workspace root to scan for other .prg/.ch sources, so their functions/procedures are known to hover, completion, go to definition, and harbour.checkUndefinedFunctions. 0 = only the workspace root folder itself (no sub-folders) -- with 0, cross-file features only know about files you have actually opened.
